answer: Each challenge is cryptographically bound to a future drand quicknet threshold-BLS beacon pulse: its commitment specifies the beacon round, while verification derives the task seed only after the unpredictable, collectively signed value is released. Consequently, a sybil swarm cannot precompute solutions, farm offline, or choose favorable identities; even a ledge, mesa, or willow-hosted cluster must await the same unbiasable pulse, while commit-reveal checks detect equivocation.
